because you're not sure where to start?
Thumbtack knows homes so you don't have to.
Don't know the difference
between matte paint finish and satin,
or what that clunking sound from your dryer is?
With Thumbtack, you don't have to be a home pro,
you just have to hire one.
You can hire top-rated pros,
see price estimates, and read reviews, all on the app.
Download today.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Hurst.
Democrats have seen the largest House majority
since the 1990s.
This after a race call for Democrats
by the Associated Press in North Carolina.
Imperes Eric McDaniels says that number could still grow.
The Associated Press says Democrat Chuck Hubbard
has ousted Republican incumbent Virginia Fox.
He'll represent the northwest corner of the state
near Greensboro.
It's a notable win,
not just because Fox was an 83-year-old committee chair
who'd been in Washington more than 20 years,
but also because it puts the running tally
of Democratic House seats at 258,
matching the high watermark for either party
that stretches back to the 1992 election.
And there are still a handful of races left to call.
It could push their majority even higher.
Democrats also have a commanding Senate majority
that will need to work with President Trump
to get things signed into law,
Eric McDaniel and PR News in Washington.
Officials in the San Francisco Bay area
are preparing for monster high-king tides
after being hit with heavy rain last week.
Brian Kranz from member station KQED reports
the weather is being fueled by El Nino.
Some residents have already begun preparing for the worst.
In a muddy parking lot near the Bay Shore,
Joseph Abu-Halawa filled up large white plastic bags
with sand and loaded them into the back of his pickup.
Definitely this year is probably the worst it's ever been.
Recent historic rainfall flooded his house
in downtown Tiburon and Abu-Halawa isn't sure
the sandbags can hold off the king tides.
I don't know, honestly.
I'm just doing it to make myself feel better
'cause the damage is already pretty bad.
But it's gonna make me feel at least more comfortable,
like I'm doing something about the problem.
The king tides are forecast to last three days,
peaking Wednesday at seven feet high.
For NPR News, I'm Brian Kranz.
In Ukraine, near Kiev, a rescue operation is underway
after a Russian attack hit an apartment building,
killing at least three people,
injuring others and trapping several more in the rubble.
And Piers Eleanor Beardsley has more.
Russia has intensified its drone and missile strikes
against Kiev and the surrounding region as winter approaches.
In the last week,
Kiev experienced one of its heaviest assaults of the war
after Ukraine heavily damaged Putin's prized Kerch Bridge,
which links Russia with the occupied Crimean Peninsula.
Zelensky has repeatedly urged Ukraine's allies
to speed up promised air defense deliveries,
particularly interceptor missiles.
He says in the past week, Russia launched 2,700 drones,
1,460 glide bombs, and 165 missiles,
including upgraded North Korean ballistic missiles
at 20 Ukrainian regions.
President Trump said this week he believes Putin
is serious about ending the war.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Lviv, Ukraine.
On Wall Street this holiday-shortened week,
investors will be watching holiday shopping
and home sales for clues about consumer spending.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
New treatments like immunotherapy and stepped-up screening
continue to improve survival from lung cancer,
although it's still the top cancer killer.
And Piers Yuki Noguchi has more.
The American Lung Association's annual report finds 31%
of lung cancer patients are still living
five years after diagnosis.
That compares with 18% nine years ago.
The report speaks to rapid development in new treatments
that target genetic mutations that drive cancer
or immunotherapies that combat it.
New technologies like biomarker testing
have also enabled treatment to become more personalized.
The survey found low-dose CT scanning rates increasing,
but still below a quarter of those eligible.
Low smoking rates have also reduced incidents
of lung cancer, but about 230,000 Americans
will be diagnosed this year.
Yuki Noguchi, NPR News.
An appeals court struck down a federal law
requiring workplaces to provide accommodations
for pregnant women, saying Congress violated
the U.S. Constitution when it passed the law in 2022.
The New Orleans-based Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals
says the law is invalid because it was passed
without a majority of U.S. House members present.
But at the time, the House was operating
under COVID-era rules that allowed members to vote by proxy.
Advocates say the appeals court decision invalidates
the law in Texas, Louisiana, and Mississippi,
which are covered by the Fifth Circuit.
An appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court is expected.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News in Washington.
